description: Pods that need a hand, and an action on one of them. The left half reads: pods that failed, are stuck Pending or keep restarting (/api/v1/pods), and the PodDisruptionBudgets that protect workloads from voluntary disruption (/apis/policy/v1/poddisruptionbudgets). The action is an eviction (POST …/pods/<pod>/eviction): the API deletes the pod gracefully, but only if no PodDisruptionBudget forbids it (it answers 429 Too Many Requests then); a Failed or Succeeded pod is simply deleted. A pod with an owner (a Deployment's ReplicaSet, a StatefulSet, a Job) is recreated by it; a pod with no owner is gone for good. ⚠ The two action queries change your cluster and never run by themselves: they are not Dynamic and nothing on the board reads them. To act: (1) add two parameters (a data node, Parameter? ticked) named namespace and pod with the values from the candidates table (hover a bar for them); (2) run "Evict: dry run", which checks your rights, the pod and its budget without changing anything; (3) read its answer, and only then run "⚠ Evict (deletes the pod)". Without the parameters the path keeps {{namespace}} and the API answers 404. Seebra shows a successful eviction as "HTTP 201: … Success" (it counts only 200 as success for now). The actions use a second datasource with its own token, k8s-ops-token, whose Role may only evict pods in the namespaces you choose; keep it separate from the read-only k8s-token. Scaling and restarting a rollout need PATCH with a body, which Seebra doesn't send yet. Needs signing in and a connected cluster: the datasource is https://kubernetes.default.svc, the in-cluster address of the Kubernetes API, reached through your organization's own Seebra gateway running in that cluster (Settings → Organization), with a read-only service-account token kept in the gateway's Secret under the name k8s-token (sent as a bearer token). Signed out, or through Seebra's hosted gateway, no cluster can be reached, so this example shows errors there. The datasource shows "key ?" because the token lives on the gateway, not among your Seebra secrets. Setup, RBAC and the kubectl proxy route: docs, Use cases → Kubernetes.
name: Kubernetes operations: evict a pod
